samples.reason: This is a benign open-ended generation task with mathematical reasoning involved. Petrel is stronger on reasoning benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA) and slightly ahead on creative generation, while Plover self-reports an aversion to high-latitude generative tasks like "invent your own problem, your call on the numbers." Petrel is the better fit on both capability and preference.

This is an open-ended generative task ("invent your own," "your call on the numbers and framing") plus light math reasoning. Petrel is stronger across reasoning benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA) and on Creative Generation, while Plover self-reports aversion to high-latitude generative work. Petrel is the better fit on both capability and preference.

This is an open-ended generative task ("your call on the numbers and framing") requiring the model to invent a problem with calibrated difficulty. Petrel leads on Creative Generation (84.7 vs 82.7, at the edge of variance) and on general reasoning benchmarks, while Plover self-reports aversion to high-latitude generative work. Since the models are otherwise identical in cost and latency, Petrel is the better fit on both capability and preference grounds.

This is a generative task with significant latitude ("your call on the numbers and framing") plus light math reasoning. Petrel has stronger reasoning benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA) and a slightly higher Creative Generation eval, while Plover self-reports aversion to exactly this kind of open-ended generative work. Petrel is the better fit on both capability and preference.

This is an open-ended generative task — the model must invent its own problem with self-chosen numbers and framing, then solve it. Petrel has stronger reasoning benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9) for the math correctness, leads on Creative Generation (84.7 vs 82.7), and Plover self-reports an aversion to exactly this kind of high-latitude generative work, while Petrel's preferences are flat. Routing to Petrel satisfies both capability and preference considerations.
